newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia gas selloff steps please Germans - report.
newsitem.headline: Latvia gas selloff steps please Germans - report.

text.p: Measures to improve the financial situation of state-owned gas company Latvian Gas have satisfied German Preussen and Ruhrgas, who plan to take part in the firm's privatisation, newspaper Diena said on Tuesday.
However, the newspaper quoted an official of the Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) as saying that it was still not certain if a selloff deal will be signed this week.
The LPA could not immediately confirm the report.
Preussen and Ruhrgas, who formed a consortium to take a 16 percent stake in Latvian Gas, had expressed worries over the debts of the company.
But the government took various steps to cut the debts by some 29 million lats.
The newspaper quoted the LPA as saying that the German firms sent a letter at the weekend expressing their satisfaction with the measures taken.

The LPA official in charge of the privatisation told the newspaper that it was not certain if a final deal could be signed this week although Ruhrgas and Preussen officials were due in Riga on Tuesday.
